title: Master Plan — LOCKED 2026-08-09 by John ("lock plus hardening fold")
claims: This planning session produced a complete, locked plan for rebuilding Anchor's project-level **steward chamber** to the "M1 Mission Flow" mockup, on top of the existing Ecgberht engine. Two documents came out of it, and both were signed off by John on 2026-08-09: a **Master Plan** (locked as "lock plus hardening fold") and a **Foreman-ready Implementation Plan**.

The Master Plan settles what the rebuilt chamber has to be. Opening the Seal must paint in under two seconds from the ledger with zero model calls, so the view is deterministic-first rather than waiting on a model to describe itself. The flow rail becomes the actual declared pipeline — typed edges between steps, one-line yields when a step finishes, the live 10-minute status table rendered inside the running step, and a declared deliverable that goes live when it lands. The steward speaks first and drives; decision points are serialized prose cards that put the question last instead of bare dialogs. The plan converts nine acceptance criteria (E1–E9) drawn from the earlier assessment into eight numbered success criteria, and it draws a hard line that the three most important ones are **engine-enforced, never model convention**: visibility injected from telemetry with a turn that structurally cannot close on an unanswered question (E1), a deterministic worktree artifact sweep before any re-commission can be proposed (E2), and a mechanical diff against the correction ledger so a resumed agent can't silently revert applied fixes (E3). Work is sequenced across five phases, 0 through 4, gate-ordered so nothing paints before its data is proven and no surface ships ahead of its own enforcement. The lock also absorbed seven single-shark hardening findings (F1–F7) as plan text — numbered criteria, a versioned JSON-schema'd manifest, execution bounds and containment checks on deliverable actions and the sweep, a DOM-injection discipline with a hostile-string CI suite, CSRF-class assertions on state-changing surfaces, and formally recording the ratified E1 question bound as a North-Star amendment so the spec and the enforcement can't drift apart.

The Implementation Plan turns that into **twelve Foreman waves** with a multi-root test command spanning both the Anchor and Ecgberht repos. Waves 1–3 are pure de-risking before anything renders: a provenance table proving every painted datum has a real source, a reachable-state matrix with one batched mockup-amendment gate for John, a seam-proof spike, the auth/CSRF fixture, and a pre-registered ease-metric classifier frozen before any surface exists so it can't be tuned to flatter the build. Waves 4–6 build the deterministic substrate and prove the two-second, zero-model-call open on a real painted surface. Waves 7–9 mount the verbatim M1 rail with a DOM-diff kill gate, land E1 with the say box, and ship the STATUS overlay. Waves 10–11 add steward drive, the serialized gate queue, preference preload and the REFINE overlay, with E2 and E3 co-landing on the surfaces they guard. Wave 12 runs the cross-criterion audit, retires the old bottom run tiles only on signed rail+STATUS parity, and closes with the ease report. The plan also expanded the success criteria to C1–C12 — adding mockup fidelity as a kill gate, engine-tested security folds, gated tile retirement, and a "build-vs-wire honesty" registry naming the ten already-built pieces that must be re-homed rather than reinvented. Finally, an independent Fable verification review traced fourteen reference-session behaviors against the gates and returned **yes-with-noted-risks**; its six findings (V1–V6) were folded in as normative amendments, closing the question-parser gap for imperative asks without question marks, turning a missing live re-brief channel into an explicit halt for John rather than a quiet downgrade, widening commit coverage to every landing, and requiring a dated real end-to-end live run plus measured spoken-turn latency, because "work never waits on John" can't be signed off from fixtures alone.

This planning session produced a locked, build-ready plan for rebuilding Anchor's project-level **steward chamber** to the "Mission Flow" (M1) mockup, running on the existing Ecgberht engine. Both documents live in `planning/steward-chamber-2026-08-09/`.

The **Master Plan** was locked by John on 2026-08-09 with the note "lock plus hardening fold." It reached that lock the honest way: two consecutive dry Shark-Tank rounds (no blocker found by two or more adversarial reviewers), after which John — the convergence authority — signed off. The North Star it settles on is a chamber that paints in under two seconds straight from the ledger with **zero model calls** on open, where the flow rail *is* the declared pipeline (typed edges between steps, one-line yields when a step finishes, the live 10-minute status table rendered inside the running step, and a declared deliverable that goes live when it lands). The steward speaks first and drives; decision gates are serialized prose cards with the question asked last, never bare dialogs. Explicit non-goals were fixed just as firmly: no engine-spine changes, no UI beyond the mockup, no portfolio-level work, no new commission lanes, and the old bottom run tiles get retired. Eight numbered success criteria (C1–C8) and the nine E-criteria from the earlier refined proposal became the acceptance bar, with three of them — visibility, sweep-before-re-pay, and the resurrection-regression guard — required to be **engine-enforced rather than model convention**, on the stated principle that convention flaps under load. The plan was then laid out as five gate-ordered phases (0 through 4), starting with pure de-risking work (data-provenance audit, reachable-state matrix, seam-proof spike) so that nothing paints before its data is proven and nothing ships ahead of its enforcement. The lock also folded in seven single-reviewer findings that didn't meet the two-shark blocker bar but were worth absorbing anyway: numbered criteria, a versioned JSON-schema'd manifest, execution bounds on deliverable run/open actions, symlink-containment checks on the artifact sweep, a DOM-injection discipline with a hostile-string CI suite, CSRF-class assertions on state-changing surfaces, and formally recording the E1 question-parse bound as a North-Star amendment so the spec and the enforcement can't drift apart. Items considered and deliberately *not* folded were recorded with reasons rather than dropped silently.

The **Implementation Plan** takes that master plan down to a Foreman-ready build, also locked 2026-08-09 — this one after a conditional approval that a Fable-driver verification review resolved as "yes, with noted risks," those risks folded back in as amendments carrying the same authority as the wave text. It expands the criteria set to C1–C12 (adding mockup fidelity as a kill gate, engine-tested security folds, tile retirement only on signed parity, and build-vs-wire honesty), and binds every criterion to a named test in a specific wave, with a re-verification pass in the final wave. A notable piece of discipline here is the **wire-homing registry**: ten capabilities that already exist — run_pulse, step_detail/step_note, status_flip, compose-first cards, reflection, the findings ledger, the live status line, paced-PTY writes, and campaign auto-commit — are listed by owner file and symbol with a committed characterization oracle each, so the build is required to re-home them rather than quietly reimplement them, and no existing code may be deleted before parity is proven. The plan spans twelve waves across the two repositories (Anchor and Ecgberht) under an explicit two-repo execution contract, including a multi-root test runner delivered in wave 1 so the gate exists from the very first commit. Waves 1–3 do the ground-truth and enforcement-infrastructure work, 4–5 build the deterministic data substrate, wave 6 is the early measured-paint milestone that blocks everything after it, and the later waves land the rail, the overlays, the gate queue, the enforcement hooks, and finally the cross-criterion audit, tile retirement, and the campaign-close ease report.

Taken together, the session moved this effort from an assessed proposal to two signed, mutually consistent documents: a locked north star with numbered acceptance criteria, and a twelve-wave build plan where every criterion has a falsifiable test, a home wave, and a re-verification row — ready to hand to Foreman.
